messages.subject: Re: [RHadoop:#702] short timeout when connecting to hbase with rhbase
parts:
Hi Simon,
sorry it took me some time to look into this. It looks like we are opening a socket  with default timeout. There is an alternative call with an explicit timeout setting. We could make that higher or user configurable. I need to discuss the consequences of this with the main rhbase developer. If it were for me, there would be no timeout, but I am sure there is a price to pay somehow. Do you have a workaround? Just calling hb.init again? Or do you have to restart the session?  Thanks

Antonio


On Thu, Mar 28, 2013 at 11:54 AM, Simon <simon...@gmail.com> wrote:
It seems like the list of functions returned by hb.scan.ex() has some type of timeout associated with it, but I'm not sure
what it is.
For example, I initiate an hbase connection and call hb.scan.ex(table, filter) and assign
the returned value to a variable called row.
I can then get 50 records by running data <- row$get(50).

This works fine; however, if I don't use 'row' for a few minutes, if I try to run data <- row$get(50) I get
an error:
Error in row$get(50) :
  rhbase<hbScannerGetList>:: (IOError) Default TException.

Is there some config file that I need to modify to change the timeout? Or is this a result of something different?
